requirements.original: The port names in a component type definition are local to that component type, i.e. another component type may have ports with the same names.
requirements.canonical: A port name in a component type definition IS local to that component type, and another component type MAY have ports with the same name.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- The port names in a component type definition are local to that component type, i.e. another component type may have ports with the same names.

requirements.original: Port names in the same component type definition shall all have unique names.
requirements.canonical: All port names in the same component type definition SHALL be unique.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether uniqueness is only among ports or among all definitions of the component type (variables, timers, ...); the general scope rules of clause 5.2 suggest the latter.
readings: All port names in the same component type definition SHALL be unique among the ports.
A port name in a component type definition SHALL be unique among all identifiers declared in that component type.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- Port names in the same component type definition shall all have unique names.

requirements.original: If not stated otherwise, ports have the same semantics as constants of a port type.
requirements.canonical: Unless stated otherwise, a component port IS having the same semantics as a constant of a port type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- If not stated otherwise, ports have the same semantics as constants of a port type.

requirements.original: It is also possible to declare constants, variables, templates and timers local to a particular component type.
requirements.canonical: A component type MAY contain declarations of constants, variables, templates and timers local to that component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- It is also possible to declare constants, variables, templates and timers local to a particular component type.

requirements.original: These declarations are visible to all testcases, functions and altsteps that run on an instance of the given component type.
requirements.canonical: The constants, variables, templates and timers declared in a component type ARE visible to all testcases, functions and altsteps that run on an instance of that component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- These declarations are visible to all testcases, functions and altsteps that run on an instance of the given component type.

requirements.original: This shall be explicitly stated using the runs on keyword (see clause 15.12) in the testcase, function or altstep header.
requirements.canonical: A testcase, function or altstep that uses the declarations of a component type SHALL explicitly state the component type in a `runs on` clause of its header.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- This shall be explicitly stated using the runs on keyword (see clause 15.12) in the testcase, function or altstep header.

requirements.original: Component type definitions are associated with the component instance and follow the scope rules defined in clause 5.2.
requirements.canonical: A component type definition IS associated with the component instance and follows the scope rules of clause 5.2.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- Component type definitions are associated with the component instance and follow the scope rules defined in clause 5.2.

requirements.original: Each new instance of a component type will thus have its own set of constants, variables, templates and timers as specified in the component type definition (including any initial values, if stated).
requirements.canonical: Each new instance of a component type IS having its own set of constants, variables, templates and timers as specified in the component type definition, including any initial values.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- Each new instance of a component type will thus have its own set of constants, variables, templates and timers as specified in the component type definition (including any initial values, if stated).

requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions of type declarations for variables, constants or ports shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10, however constants used in the constant expressions of initial values for variables, constants, templates or timers do not have to obey these restrictions.
requirements.canonical: A constant used in the constant expression of a type declaration for a component variable, constant or port SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.

ambiguity.issue: 'type declarations' presumably means constant expressions within the type part of a declaration (e.g. array dimensions, length restrictions); the restrictions of clause 10 are not named explicitly.
readings: A constant used in a constant expression within the type of a component variable, constant or port declaration (e.g. array size) SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
A constant used in any constant expression of a component variable, constant or port declaration, except its initial value, SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- Constants used in the constant expressions of type declarations for variables, constants or ports shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10, however constants used in the constant expressions of initial values for variables, constants, templates or timers do not have to obey these restrictions.

requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions of type declarations for variables, constants or ports shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10, however constants used in the constant expressions of initial values for variables, constants, templates or timers do not have to obey these restrictions.
requirements.canonical: A constant used in the constant expression of an initial value for a component variable, constant, template or timer NEED NOT obey the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- Constants used in the constant expressions of type declarations for variables, constants or ports shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10, however constants used in the constant expressions of initial values for variables, constants, templates or timers do not have to obey these restrictions.

requirements.original: type component ComponentTypeIdentifier "{" { ( PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) } "}"
requirements.canonical: A component type definition has the syntax `type component` ComponentTypeIdentifier "{" { PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef } "}".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- type component ComponentTypeIdentifier "{" { ( PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) } "}"

requirements.original: Component type definitions specify the creation, declaration and initialization of ports and component constants, variables, templates and timers during the creation of an instance of a component type.
requirements.canonical: A component type definition IS specifying the creation, declaration and initialization of ports, component constants, variables, templates and timers during the creation of an instance of the component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- Component type definitions specify the creation, declaration and initialization of ports and component constants, variables, templates and timers during the creation of an instance of a component type.

requirements.original: These instances can be used as the main test component, as the test system interface or as a parallel test component.
requirements.canonical: An instance of a component type MAY be used as the main test component, as the test system interface or as a parallel test component.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- These instances can be used as the main test component, as the test system interface or as a parallel test component.

requirements.original: Every instance of a component type has its own new instances of the ports, constants, variables, templates and timers defined in the component type definition.
requirements.canonical: Every instance of a component type IS having its own new instances of the ports, constants, variables, templates and timers defined in the component type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- Every instance of a component type has its own new instances of the ports, constants, variables, templates and timers defined in the component type definition.

requirements.original: Component instances are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.
requirements.canonical: A component instance IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.

ambiguity.issue: 'Component instances are object references' conflates the component and the reference value to it; 'specific rules' are not referenced.
readings: A component reference value IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
A component instance itself IS an object, referenced through object references.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- Component instances are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.

requirements.original: type component MyCompType { port MyMessagePortType pCOm[3]; port MyProcedurePortType pCOp[3][3] // Defines a component type which has an array of 3 message ports and a two-dimensional // array of 9 procedure ports. }
requirements.canonical: A component type MAY declare port arrays, including multi-dimensional port arrays.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.1 -- type component MyCompType { port MyMessagePortType pCOm[3]; port MyProcedurePortType pCOp[3][3] // Defines a component type which has an array of 3 message ports and a two-dimensional // array of 9 procedure ports. }

requirements.original: It is possible to define component types as the extension of other component types, using the extends keyword.
requirements.canonical: A component type MAY be defined as the extension of other component types using the `extends` keyword.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- It is possible to define component types as the extension of other component types, using the extends keyword.

requirements.original: type component ComponentTypeIdentifier extends ComponentTypeIdentifier { "," ComponentTypeIdentifier} "{" { ( PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) } "}"
requirements.canonical: A component type extension has the syntax `type component` ComponentTypeIdentifier `extends` ComponentTypeIdentifier { "," ComponentTypeIdentifier } "{" { PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef } "}".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- type component ComponentTypeIdentifier extends ComponentTypeIdentifier { "," ComponentTypeIdentifier} "{" { ( PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef ) } "}"

requirements.original: The effect of this definition is that the extended type will implicitly also contain all definitions from the supertype.
requirements.canonical: An extended component type IS implicitly containing all definitions from its supertype.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- The effect of this definition is that the extended type will implicitly also contain all definitions from the supertype.

requirements.original: It is allowed to have one component type extending several supertypes in one definition, which have to be specified as a comma-separated list of types in the definition.
requirements.canonical: A component type MAY extend several supertypes in one definition, specified as a comma-separated list of component types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- It is allowed to have one component type extending several supertypes in one definition, which have to be specified as a comma-separated list of types in the definition.

requirements.original: Any of the supertypes may also be defined by means of extension.
requirements.canonical: A supertype of a component type extension MAY itself be defined by means of extension.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- Any of the supertypes may also be defined by means of extension.

requirements.original: The effective component type definition of the extended type is obtained as the collection of all constant, variable, template, timer and port definitions contributed by the supertypes (determined recursively if a supertype is also defined by means of an extension) and the definitions declared in the extended type directly.
requirements.canonical: The effective component type definition of an extended type IS the collection of all constant, variable, template, timer and port definitions contributed by the supertypes, determined recursively, and the definitions declared directly in the extended type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- The effective component type definition of the extended type is obtained as the collection of all constant, variable, template, timer and port definitions contributed by the supertypes (determined recursively if a supertype is also defined by means of an extension) and the definitions declared in the extended type directly.

requirements.original: The effective component type definition shall be name clash free.
requirements.canonical: The effective component type definition SHALL be free of name clashes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- The effective component type definition shall be name clash free.

requirements.original: NOTE 1: It is not considered to be a different declaration and hence causes no error if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type by different supertypes (via different extension paths).
requirements.canonical: A definition contributed to the extended type by different supertypes via different extension paths IS NOT a different declaration and causes no error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- NOTE 1: It is not considered to be a different declaration and hence causes no error if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type by different supertypes (via different extension paths).

requirements.original: The semantics of component types with extensions are defined by simply replacing each component type definition by its effective component type definition as a pre-processing step prior to using it.
requirements.canonical: The semantics of a component type with extensions IS defined by replacing each component type definition with its effective component type definition as a pre-processing step before use.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- The semantics of component types with extensions are defined by simply replacing each component type definition by its effective component type definition as a pre-processing step prior to using it.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: For component type compatibility, this means that a component reference c of type CT1, which extends CT2, is compatible with CT2, and test cases, functions and altsteps specifying CT2 in their runs `on` clauses can be executed on c (see clause 6.3.2.7).
requirements.canonical: A component reference of a component type CT1 that extends CT2 IS compatible with CT2, and testcases, functions and altsteps with `runs on` CT2 CAN be executed on it.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- NOTE 2: For component type compatibility, this means that a component reference c of type CT1, which extends CT2, is compatible with CT2, and test cases, functions and altsteps specifying CT2 in their runs `on` clauses can be executed on c (see clause 6.3.2.7).

requirements.original: a) When defining component types by extension, there shall be no name clash between the definitions being taken from the supertype and the definitions being added in the extended type, i.e. there shall not be a port, variable, constant or timer identifier that is declared both in the supertype (directly or by means of extension) and the extended type.
requirements.canonical: When defining a component type by extension, a port, variable, constant or timer identifier SHALL NOT be declared both in the supertype (directly or by means of extension) and in the extended type.

ambiguity.issue: The list 'port, variable, constant or timer' omits templates, although templates are part of component type definitions and of the effective definition (s008).
readings: A port, variable, constant, timer or template identifier SHALL NOT be declared both in the supertype and the extended type.
Only port, variable, constant and timer identifiers SHALL NOT be declared both in the supertype and the extended type.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- a) When defining component types by extension, there shall be no name clash between the definitions being taken from the supertype and the definitions being added in the extended type, i.e. there shall not be a port, variable, constant or timer identifier that is declared both in the supertype (directly or by means of extension) and the extended type.

requirements.original: It is not considered to be a name clash if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type via different extension paths.
requirements.canonical: A definition contributed to the extended type via different extension paths IS NOT a name clash between the supertype and the extended type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- It is not considered to be a name clash if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type via different extension paths.

requirements.original: b) When defining component types by extending more than one parent type, there shall be no name clash between the definitions of the different supertypes, i.e. there shall not be a port, variable, constant or timer identifier that is declared in any two of the supertypes (directly or by means of extension).
requirements.canonical: When defining a component type by extending more than one supertype, a port, variable, constant or timer identifier SHALL NOT be declared in any two of the supertypes (directly or by means of extension).

ambiguity.issue: Templates are omitted from the list of definitions; 'parent type' is used for supertype.
readings: A port, variable, constant, timer or template identifier SHALL NOT be declared in any two supertypes.
Only port, variable, constant and timer identifiers SHALL NOT be declared in any two supertypes.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- b) When defining component types by extending more than one parent type, there shall be no name clash between the definitions of the different supertypes, i.e. there shall not be a port, variable, constant or timer identifier that is declared in any two of the supertypes (directly or by means of extension).

requirements.original: It is not considered to be a name clash if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type via different extension paths.
requirements.canonical: A definition contributed to the extended type via different extension paths IS NOT a name clash between different supertypes.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- It is not considered to be a name clash if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type via different extension paths.

requirements.original: c) It is allowed to extend component types that are defined by means of extension, as long as no cyclic chain of definition is created.
requirements.canonical: A component type defined by means of extension MAY itself be extended.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- c) It is allowed to extend component types that are defined by means of extension, as long as no cyclic chain of definition is created.

requirements.original: c) It is allowed to extend component types that are defined by means of extension, as long as no cyclic chain of definition is created.
requirements.canonical: A component type extension SHALL NOT create a cyclic chain of definitions.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.10.2 -- c) It is allowed to extend component types that are defined by means of extension, as long as no cyclic chain of definition is created.

requirements.original: system | mtc | self | ObjectReference
requirements.canonical: A component reference IS syntactically one of `system`, `mtc`, `self` or an ObjectReference.

examples.text:
var MyComponentType v_myAddress; 
  v_myAddress := self; // Store the current component reference

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- system | mtc | self | ObjectReference

requirements.original: A unique component reference is generated by the test system at the time when a component is created.
requirements.canonical: The test system SHALL generate a unique component reference at the time a test component is created.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- A unique component reference is generated by the test system at the time when a component is created.

requirements.original: It is the result of a create operation (see clause 21.2.1).
requirements.canonical: The `create` operation IS returning the unique component reference of the created test component.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- It is the result of a create operation (see clause 21.2.1).

requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).
requirements.canonical: The `system` operation IS returning the component reference of the test system interface.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).
requirements.canonical: The `mtc` operation IS returning the component reference of the MTC.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).
requirements.canonical: The MTC IS created automatically when testcase execution is started.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).
requirements.canonical: The `self` operation IS returning the component reference of the test component in which `self` is called.

examples.text:
var MyComponentType v_myAddress; 
  v_myAddress := self; // Store the current component reference

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.original: Component references are used in the configuration operations such as connect, map and start (see clause 21) to set-up test configurations and in the from, to and sender parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface for addressing purposes (see clause 22 and figure 6).
requirements.canonical: A component reference MAY be used in configuration operations such as `connect`, `map` and `start` to set up test configurations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- Component references are used in the configuration operations such as connect, map and start (see clause 21) to set-up test configurations and in the from, to and sender parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface for addressing purposes (see clause 22 and figure 6).

requirements.original: Component references are used in the configuration operations such as connect, map and start (see clause 21) to set-up test configurations and in the from, to and sender parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface for addressing purposes (see clause 22 and figure 6).
requirements.canonical: A component reference MAY be used for addressing in the `from`, `to` and `sender` parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- Component references are used in the configuration operations such as connect, map and start (see clause 21) to set-up test configurations and in the from, to and sender parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface for addressing purposes (see clause 22 and figure 6).

requirements.original: In addition, the special value null is available to indicate an undefined component reference, e.g. for the initialization of variables to handle component references.
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` MAY be used to indicate an undefined component reference, e.g. to initialize a variable of a component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- In addition, the special value null is available to indicate an undefined component reference, e.g. for the initialization of variables to handle component references.

requirements.original: A component reference includes component type information.
requirements.canonical: A component reference IS carrying the component type information of the referenced test component.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- A component reference includes component type information.

requirements.original: This means, for example, that a variable for handling component references shall use the corresponding component type name in its declaration.
requirements.canonical: A variable for handling component references SHALL be declared with the corresponding component type name as its type.

examples.text:
var MyComponentType v_myAddress; 
  v_myAddress := self; // Store the current component reference

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- This means, for example, that a variable for handling component references shall use the corresponding component type name in its declaration.

requirements.original: The configuration operations (see clause 21) do not work directly on arrays of components.
requirements.canonical: A configuration operation SHALL NOT be applied directly to an array of component references.

ambiguity.issue: 'arrays of components' is used, but TTCN-3 only has arrays of component references.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- The configuration operations (see clause 21) do not work directly on arrays of components.

requirements.original: Instead a specific element of the array shall be provided as the parameter to these operations.
requirements.canonical: When a configuration operation refers to a test component held in an array of component references, a specific element of the array SHALL be provided as the parameter of the operation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- Instead a specific element of the array shall be provided as the parameter to these operations.

requirements.original: For components, the effect of an array is achieved by using an array of component references and assigning the relevant array element to the result of the create operation.
requirements.canonical: The effect of an array of test components CAN be achieved by using an array of component references and assigning the result of a `create` operation to each relevant array element.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- For components, the effect of an array is achieved by using an array of component references and assigning the relevant array element to the result of the create operation.

requirements.original: a) The only operations allowed on component references are assignment, equality and non-equality.
requirements.canonical: An operator other than assignment, equality (`==`) and non-equality (`!=`) SHALL NOT be applied to a component reference.

ambiguity.issue: 'operations' is read as expression operators; component operations such as start, stop, done or running are also applied to component references and are defined in clause 21, so a literal reading would contradict them.
readings: An operator other than assignment, equality (`==`) and non-equality (`!=`) SHALL NOT be applied to a component reference.
No operation other than assignment, equality and non-equality (including component operations like `start` or `done`) SHALL be applied to a component reference.

examples.text:
var MyComponentType v_myAddress; 
  v_myAddress := self; // Store the current component reference

requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- a) The only operations allowed on component references are assignment, equality and non-equality.

requirements.original: b) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a component reference SHALL be of a component type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- b) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.original: b) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a component reference SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 6.2.11 -- b) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.
